findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-anchor the lint's canonical-seam definition on the store WRITE LOCK (I5) / `event_append`+`ticket_txn` (locked, pathspec-scoped), not on `run_git_write` — which is only an index.lock self-heal and does not hold the write lock; state that the failure message must name the locked write APIs, and confirm a whole-index/`-a`/`-A` commit even through run_git_write is still flagged.
evidence: gitutil.py:239-256 run_git_write is an index.lock + HEAD-parse retry wrapper over run_git; it acquires NO store write lock
_store/lock.py:1-5 'The ONE write lock for the tickets store … invariant I5' held by ticket_txn / event_append.write_lock
Bug 3435 root cause: 'a store write OUTSIDE the unified write lock with a whole-index commit'; fix 'route the deletion through the canonical locked, pathspec-scoped event_append.delete_events'
Bug 4dd2 AC: '_prune_bridge routes through the unified store write lock (no raw unlocked git add -A + git commit)'
findings.finding: The plan names `run_git_write` as the canonical write seam the lint enforces, but `run_git_write` does NOT take the unified store write lock (I5) — it only self-heals git's index.lock/HEAD-parse faults over `run_git`. The cited bugs (3435, 4dd2) were unlocked WHOLE-INDEX commits (no write lock, no pathspec) and were fixed by routing through the locked, pathspec-scoped `event_append.delete_events` / the write lock — not through `run_git_write`. A `git commit -A` routed through `run_git_write` would PASS this lint yet reproduce the exact I5-violating race that caused those bugs, so the lint's predicate is a proxy that misses the real invariant.
scenarios: A new maintenance path calls run_git_write(tracker, 'commit', '-a', ...) — lint passes, but it is an unlocked whole-index commit that races locked writers exactly like 3435/4dd2
findings.suggested_fix: Define the seam as the write-lock-holding path (ticket_txn / event_append.write_lock / delete_events), and have the lint flag any tracker-targeted add/commit/rm/mv/update-ref that is not inside that locked, pathspec-scoped path — including whole-index (`-a`/`-A`) commits that skip a pathspec.

findings.finding: The plan gives no POSITIVE rationale for choosing a text-scan + external allowlist file over structurally different alternatives (an AST-based Python lint that resolves callees and keys on tracker constants; or a code-layer/unit-test contract that any tracker mutation must hold the write lock, mirroring how test_module_size_contract mirrors the module-size gate). It cites the module-size precedent for the config/teaching shape only, not for why this detection strategy fits. Given the shell/YAML static-detection gap, an AST lint for the Python surface would materially cut false positives/negatives.
scenarios: Implementer builds a brittle substring scanner when an AST lint (Python) + narrowly-scoped scan (shell/YAML) would be more robust

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the known live workflow-YAML bypass at `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:290-291` and state its resolution (allowlist-with-reason vs. a shell-callable seam), since `run_git_write` is Python-only and cannot be invoked from a bare YAML shell step.
evidence: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:289-291 — 'if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then / git add -A / git commit -m "chore: sync events from rebar reconciler ..."' inside `cd .tickets-tracker`
reconcile-bridge.yml:272-276 step name 'Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets' — a legitimate CI store write, i.e. a real seam-bypass decision (route vs. allowlist)
run_git_write is a Python API (gitutil.py:239) with no shell entrypoint enumerated in the plan
findings.finding: The plan's scope ('remediation of any bypass sites the first full scan finds') and AC ('Tree is clean at landing') do not enumerate a concrete, currently-live in-scope bypass: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:290-291` runs raw `git add -A` + `git commit` against the `.tickets-tracker` worktree inside a workflow shell step. This is exactly the workflow-YAML class the lint targets, and remediating it is non-trivial: a bare YAML shell step cannot directly call the Python `run_git_write` API, so it must either be allowlisted with justification or given a new shell-callable seam — an unstated design decision the 'tree is clean at landing' AC depends on.
findings.location: Scope ('remediation of any bypass sites the first full scan finds') and AC line 'Tree is clean at landing (all existing bypasses routed or allowlisted with justification)'
scenarios: The first full scan flags reconcile-bridge.yml and the author must decide route-vs-allowlist mid-implementation with no plan guidance, because run_git_write is Python-only and the step is a shell command in YAML.
Landing is blocked or a hasty un-justified allowlist entry is added to make the tree clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Add reconcile-bridge.yml to the Scope's known-sites list and decide up front whether it gets an allowlist entry (with reason: reconciler event sync in a CI-only worktree) or a shell entrypoint that wraps run_git_write; note that workflow-YAML enforcement requires such an entrypoint or the lint will have no route to offer.
